details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:509-580 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The read-budget check at line 512 runs only for runs whose `head_sha != merge_sha`, and the failure-path jobs read at line 573 is never checked against `MAX_READS_PER_HEAL`. So when earlier unrelated runs have each used a compare read, picking a failure on the merge commit makes the jobs read the 4th REST read for that heal.
  WHY: This breaks the linked issue's acceptance criterion and the documented "at most 3 REST reads per heal" limit (script header lines 48-52, agents.d/heal-verify.md, changelog.d/heal-verify.md). Two paths reach 4 reads: page + window + an unrelated `success` compare + a merge-commit failure, or list + two unrelated `success` compares + a merge-commit failure. No test covers either ordering. All reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:413 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The GraphQL list query hardcodes first:50, which causes it to miss heal issues beyond the first 50 updated in the last 7 days.
  WHY: Older heal issues still inside the 7-day verification window are ignored, so regressions can go unverified.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:468-514 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The window read now counts toward `MAX_READS_PER_HEAL=3`, and the `read_limit=$((MAX_READS_PER_HEAL + 1))` allowance was removed. On a cut-off runs list, a failed run on a descendant commit therefore needs compare plus jobs (more than 3 reads) and returns `outcome=pending reason=read_budget` on every tick.
  WHY: Truncation is permanent for that heal, so a fix that recurred on a busy workflow is never reopened inside the 7-day window. The prior design handled this case, and the "fail open, retry next hour" comment (line 473) is misleading. The test at tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_verify.py:439 locks this behaviour in. The reviewer rated it MAJOR.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_verify.py:169 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Every test fixture hard-codes `hasNextPage: False`, and the fake `gh` ignores the `first:` argument, so neither the `warn reason=list_truncated` handler (lines 211-212) nor the issue-list truncation consequences are exercised.
  WHY: An accidental change to the query limit, or a truncation bug, would not be caught by the suite. The reviewer rated it NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Identify heal issues the same way existing heal scripts do (label or markers)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh `LIST_QUERY` (line 413) and closed-heal candidate selection
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The query at line 413 filters only on `labels:["ai:workflow-heal"]` (both `closed:` and `open:`), while `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3900 is_heal_route` accepts the label OR a body match of `HEAL_FP_RE` (fp marker). Marker-identified heals that lack the label are never selected.
- requirement: "Make one GraphQL query for qualifying closed heal issues from the last seven days" / "Budget: 1 list query per tick, then at most 3 reads per heal."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh `LIST_QUERY` (line 413) and the closed-issue candidate selection loop
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `LIST_QUERY` hardcodes `issues(first:50,...)`, lines 211-212 only log `warn reason=list_truncated` when `hasNextPage` is true, and no pagination or cursor tracking exists. The `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`-based `START` rotation (lines 445-446) rotates only within the returned list, and a pending heal can be pushed past the 50 newest `UPDATED_AT DESC` results and age out unverified.
- requirement: "When an open heal in the same lineage (same `root=` marker) was created after `mergedAt`, comment on the closed heal linking to it, and do not reopen."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh open-heal query (line 413) and `trusted_open` / lineage selection (lines 217-225, 319-323)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The open heal connection is limited to `first:50` (`CREATED_AT DESC`), and `cmd_select` searches only those nodes at lines 217-225 and 319-323. A matching lineage heal outside that page is missed, so the closed heal is wrongly reopened with `## Fix did not hold` instead of getting a `recurred_lineage` comment.
- requirement: "Budget: 1 list query per tick, then at most 3 reads per heal."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh `_verify_one` (the jobs read at line 573), plus a matching test in tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_verify.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: Nothing guards the jobs read against `MAX_READS_PER_HEAL`. The budget tests (`test_budget_one_list_query_and_at_most_three_reads_per_heal`, `test_compare_plus_jobs_path_stays_within_three_reads`, `test_truncated_list_descendant_failure_stays_within_three_reads`) only cover orderings where the deciding run is itself compared, and none covers an earlier unrelated compare followed by a failure on the merge commit.
- requirement: "Take the oldest completed run whose `head_sha` equals the merge commit or descends from it" and determine whether it failed at the same step, while staying within the three-read limit.
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh truncated-runs handling and run-selection budget check
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: On a truncated runs list, lines 482-495 use two reads to build the run window. For an oldest decisive failure on a descendant SHA, lines 509-514 then stop at `read_budget`, and later ticks repeat this pending result until the heal leaves the seven-day window.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:510-512, 573 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In `_verify_one`, `need` reserves a jobs read only for the run being compared. A decisive run on the merge commit (`head_sha == merge_sha`) skips the budget check, and the jobs read at line 573 always runs. Two paths reach reads=4: page + window + an unrelated success compare (`skip_run ... reason=unrelated_commit`) + a merge-commit failure, or list + two unrelated success compares + a merge-commit failure.
  WHY: One heal uses 4 REST reads, which breaks the "at most 3 reads per heal" acceptance criterion and the limit stated in the script header (lines 48-52), agents.d/heal-verify.md and changelog.d/heal-verify.md. `test_truncated_runs_list_reads_from_the_merge_to_the_oldest_run_on_the_page` and `test_unrelated_older_commit_is_skipped` do not cover this ordering. Suggested fix: add a `$((reads + 1)) -gt MAX_READS_PER_HEAL` guard before line 573 that logs `outcome=pending ... reason=read_budget`, or use `need=2` for unrelated compares, plus a test.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Requirement: "Budget: 1 list query per tick, then at most 3 reads per heal."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh `_verify_one` (the jobs read at line 573), plus a matching test in tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_verify.py.
  Evidence of absence: Nothing guards the jobs read against `MAX_READS_PER_HEAL`. The budget tests only cover orderings where the deciding run is itself compared, and none covers an earlier unrelated compare followed by a failure on the merge commit.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: Older heal issues that still fall within the 7-day verification window are ignored, potentially leaving regressions unverified.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:509-537, 572-580 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The read-budget check at line 512 sits inside `if [ "${head_sha}" != "${merge_sha}" ]`, so a run on the merge SHA is set as `picked_id` (line 538) without a budget check, and the jobs read at line 573 increments `reads`/`TOTAL_READS` without consulting `MAX_READS_PER_HEAL`. Trace: page=1, window=2, a success on OTHER_SHA compare (behind, skip_run, reads=3), a failure on MERGE_SHA picked, then the jobs read makes reads=4.
  WHY: This breaks the documented "at most 3 REST reads per heal" budget, and the final tick line logs `reads=4`. It is reachable in production on a high-traffic workflow.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Requirement: "Make one GraphQL query for heal issues authored by the pipeline login: identify heal issues the same way existing heal scripts do (label or markers), `CLOSED`, closed in the last 7 days."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh LIST_QUERY (line 413) and the candidate-selection filter
  Evidence of absence: The query filters only on `labels:["ai:workflow-heal"]`, while `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3900 is_heal_route` accepts the label OR the `HEAL_FP_RE` body marker. Heals that lost the label but carry the FP marker are never considered.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Requirement: "Budget: 1 list query per tick, then at most 3 reads per heal." (with the closed-heal list scoped to the last 7 days).
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh LIST_QUERY (line 413) and the closed-issue selection loop
  Evidence of absence: `LIST_QUERY` hardcodes `first:50`, and lines 211-212 only log `warn reason=list_truncated` without paging or rotating. When more than 50 heals close within 7 days, the remainder are silently dropped and age out unverified.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_verify.sh:509-539, 572-575 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The run-selection loop can exceed the required three REST reads per heal. It checks the remaining budget for a run only when that run's SHA differs from the merge SHA, and the jobs read that follows has no budget check.
  WHY: After the runs-list read, two earlier `success` runs on different SHAs can each use a compare read and be skipped as unrelated. A later failure on the merge SHA then bypasses the check, and the jobs request becomes the 4th read.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  Requirement: "Identify heal issues the same way existing heal scripts do (label or markers)."
  Expected change site: scripts/workf
